Yes — this is exactly what Next.js App Router's **partial prefetching** is designed for. For dynamic routes like `/projects/[id]`, the default `` only fetches the route tree down to the nearest `loading.tsx` (or ``) boundary. So structure the project page so the title lives **above** that boundary and the slow data lives **below** it. `app/projects/[id]/page.tsx` ```tsx import { getProjectMeta } from './data' // cheap, cached query import { getProjectDetails } from './data' // slow query export default async function ProjectPage({ params }) { const { id } = await params const meta = await getProjectMeta(id) // resolves during prefetch return ( <>

{meta.title}

// ready instantly on navigation }> // fetched on demand ) } ``` `app/projects/[id]/loading.tsx` ```tsx export default function Loading() { return } ``` How it behaves on hover / in viewport: - Next.js prefetches `loading.tsx` + everything above it (`meta.title`) — that's all. - The slow `` component is **not** in the prefetch response, because it sits behind the `loading.tsx` boundary. - On click, the title paints immediately from the cache; the rest streams in after. Two extra levers worth knowing: 1. Turn off the prefetch entirely if even the title is too expensive: ``. 2. For deeper control, opt into the new model in `next.config.js`: ```js module.exports = { experimental: { partialPrefetching: true } } ``` With that on, `prefetch="auto"` (the default) prefetches the per-route **app shell** — only the static and cached parts of the route — regardless of where `loading.tsx` is. The title is included iff it comes from cached data; uncached dynamic content is excluded. Docs: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching Rule of thumb: keep the cheap, cached "header" of the page in the segment itself, and push everything expensive behind a `` or `loading.tsx`. The Link does the rest.
